The concession auction will take place on October 7, 2026, at 12:00 PM, at the headquarters of the Curtici Arad Free Zone Administration, located at 5 Iulian Grozescu Street, Arad Municipality. Applicants shall submit their applications for participation at the headquarters of the Autonomous Regime. The application must include: the name/denomination of the applicant/company, address/headquarters, telephone/fax/email number, the asset intended for concession, the activities to be carried out, and the requested duration of the concession. Applications for participation in the auction shall be submitted between August 26, 2026, and September 15, 2026, by 4:00 PM. For additional information, please contact us at the headquarters of R.A. https://www.dw.com/en/yemen-launches-maj.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5Nkh9 The escalation between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis has revived Yemen’s civil war after a four-year ceasefire [FILE: September 27, 2026] Image: Social Media/REUTERS Advertisement Yemen's Saudi-backed government on Sunday announced a new military operation to retake territory held by Iran-backed Houthi rebels , as fighting intensified around the key southwestern city of Taiz. "Today, I announce the start of military operations to retake the remaining territory of the republic and extend the authority of the state and its institutions across the entire national territory," Yemeni Presidential Council chief Rashad al-Alimi said in a televised address. The announcement came after Houthi fighters captured a key road linking Taiz with the government-held city of Aden, effectively isolating Taiz. The rebels have besieged Taiz for more than a decade. More than 70 people were reportedly killed in fighting around Taiz over the past day, according to AFP news agency. Can Yemen's government turn the tide against the Houthis? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video How did the conflict between Saudi Arabia and Houthis escalate? The latest developments come amid an escalation between the Houthis and the internationally recognized government in Yemen that is supported by Saudi Arabia, reviving Yemen's civil war after a four-year ceasefire. A 2022 truce between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia collapsed in July after the rebels allowed an Iranian plane to land in Yemen's capital Sanaa, which defied the Saudis' control over Yemeni airspace. As a result of the escalation, the Houthis announced a maritime blockade on Saudi Arabia. Last month, the Houthis seized Yemen's Red Sea coast and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait — a vital global shipping route — from government hands, even as Al-Alimi called for support from the international community. The Houthis have controlled Sanaa and much of Yemen's more populous western areas since the start of Yemen's civil war in 2014. Why can't the Saudis defeat the Houthis?
